title: Wisteria Wonderland, Ghibli & Meiji Shrine
description: The grand finale packs in three bucket-list experiences: sunrise wisteria at Ashikaga Flower Park (peak bloom!), the magical Ghibli Museum, and sacred Meiji Shrine with trendy Harajuku. A long but unforgettable day before your evening flight.

activities.title: Ashikaga Flower Park — Peak Wisteria
activities.description: Leave Kawaguchiko early and head to Ashikaga via train (Kawaguchiko → Otsuki → Ashikaga, ~3 hours with transfers). Late April is PEAK wisteria season — the park's 150-year-old Great Wisteria tree creates a breathtaking purple canopy. The park extends hours during wisteria season (7:00 AM opening). This is one of Japan's most spectacular seasonal sights.
details: 💰 ¥2,100/person during wisteria season (variable pricing)
⏰ Opens 7:00 during wisteria season · Allow 2 hours
📍 JR Ashikaga Flower Park Station (1 min walk)
📷 The tunnel of white and purple wisteria is jaw-dropping
⚠️ GOLDEN WEEK + WISTERIA = extremely crowded. Arrive at 7:00 opening for best experience
🚂 Route: Kawaguchiko → [bus] → Otsuki → [JR Chuo] → Takao → [JR] → Kita-Senju → [Tobu/JR] → Ashikagaflowerpark (~3h total)

meals.name: Ekiben on the Train
meals.description: Grab a vegetarian-friendly ekiben (train bento) or konbini breakfast for the journey. Inari sushi bento is a safe bet.

tips.text: Ashikaga wisteria in late April is genuinely one of the most beautiful things I have ever seen. Get there at opening — by 10am it's shoulder to shoulder.
💡 Alternative route: Take the highway bus back to Shinjuku from Kawaguchiko first (2h), then train to Ashikaga (1.5h). Slightly faster and you can store luggage at Shinjuku coin lockers.

timeBlocks.label: 🎬 Midday — Ghibli Museum + Edo-Tokyo Open Air Museum

activities.title: Ghibli Museum — Mitaka
activities.description: From Ashikaga, train to Mitaka (via Kita-Senju/Shinjuku, ~2h). The Ghibli Museum is Studio Ghibli's whimsical museum designed by Miyazaki himself — no photos allowed inside, which makes it feel like entering another world. The rooftop garden has a life-size Robot Soldier from Laputa.
details: 💰 ¥1,000/person (advance reservation ONLY — ghibli-museum.jp)
⏰ Entry times: 10:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00 — book the 14:00 slot
📍 15 min walk from Mitaka Station through Inokashira Park
⚠️ CRITICAL: Tickets sell out within minutes of release (10th of each month for next month). Book by March 10 for April entry!
🎬 Allow 1.5-2 hours

activities.title: Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum (Alternative)
activities.description: If Ghibli tickets are sold out (very possible for Golden Week), the Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum in nearby Koganei is a fantastic alternative and on your bookmarked list! Beautifully preserved historical buildings from Edo through Showa era — the bathhouse inspired Spirited Away's setting. Open-air, spacious, less crowded.
details: 💰 ¥400/person
⏰ 9:30-17:30 · Closed Mon (but open during Golden Week)
📍 Koganei Park, 5 min bus from Musashi-Koganei Station
🏘️ 30 relocated buildings spanning 400 years of Japanese architecture
🎬 The Kodakara-yu bathhouse literally inspired the bathhouse in Spirited Away

meals.name: Straw Hat Café (Ghibli Museum) or Park Picnic
meals.description: The Ghibli Museum's Straw Hat Café serves simple meals — check for veggie options (usually a pasta or curry). Alternatively, pick up konbini bento and picnic in beautiful Inokashira Park.
meals.meta: 📍 Inside Ghibli Museum or Inokashira Park · 💰 ¥800-1,200/person

tips.text: 🎫 Ghibli tickets for Golden Week are extremely hard to get. Have the Edo-Tokyo Open Air Museum as your backup — it's honestly just as magical in a different way.

activities.title: Meiji Shrine & Yoyogi Park
activities.description: Train from Mitaka/Koganei to Harajuku (JR Chuo → Shinjuku → Yamanote to Harajuku, 30-40 min). Walk through the massive torii gate into Meiji Shrine's forested grounds — 100 hectares of ancient forest in the heart of Tokyo. Write a wish on an ema (wooden plaque), see the sake barrel display, and absorb the peaceful atmosphere. Adjacent Yoyogi Park is where Tokyo's subcultures gather on weekends.
details: 💰 FREE entry (shrine) · Ema plaque: ¥500
⏰ Sunrise to sunset (roughly 5:00-18:30 in late April)
🌳 The forest walk from the torii to the shrine takes 10-15 min
📷 The main torii gate is Japan's largest wooden torii — stunning

activities.title: Harajuku & Takeshita Street
activities.description: After Meiji Shrine, cross the bridge to Harajuku's Takeshita Street — Tokyo's youth fashion capital. Colorful shops, crepe stands, and people-watching. Even if fashion isn't your thing, the energy is infectious and the street is only a few blocks long.
details: 💰 Free to browse · Crepes: ¥400-600
⏰ Shops open 11:00-20:00
💡 Omotesando Avenue nearby is the upscale counterpart — beautiful zelkova tree-lined boulevard

meals.name: Saido — Asakusa (or Ain Soph Ginza)
meals.description: If you have time before heading to the airport, Saido in Asakusa offers exquisite vegan Japanese cuisine — think plant-based sushi, tempura, and seasonal kaiseki courses. Alternatively, Ain Soph Ginza is closer to Tokyo Station.

meals.name: Haneda Airport
meals.description: Grab a final treat at Haneda's terminal — the T's TanTan outpost at Haneda Terminal 3 (international) serves the same excellent vegan ramen. Perfect last meal in Japan.

tips.text: ✈️ Leave for Haneda by 16:30 at the latest. Keikyu Line from Shinagawa takes ~25 min. Your 19:40 flight needs check-in by ~17:30.
🛍️ Last-minute souvenirs: Haneda airport has excellent shopping — Tokyo Banana, matcha KitKats, and wagashi (traditional sweets) are all vegetarian-safe.
